fieldMarks: Winter: white with black tail feathers; feet heavily feathered to the toes.
Breeding male: chestnut head and neck on a white body, becoming mostly reddish-brown with white wings.
Female: duller mottled brown through summer.
Males raise red combs in display.
behavior: Courting males give a loud, staccato go-back, go-back.
Walks and picks at willow, alder and birch buds, leaves and twigs, and berries; swallows grit.
Less migratory than rock ptarmigan but sometimes winters south of the breeding range; populations cycle.
habitat: Tundra, willow scrub and muskeg north of treeline, especially low wet tundra with dwarf willow thickets; also near treeline in mountains.

lookalikes.name: Rock ptarmigan
lookalikes.howToTell: Rock ptarmigan is smaller with a smaller bill; the winter male has a black eye line.
